To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) A type discipline can be given for a skeletal higher order module language, which has principal signatures; (2) Sharing is handled in a manner that is compatible with the ML modules semantics; (3) The type system is decidable; (4) A type inference algorithm is given.

- A higher-order module system is possible, and can be given a type discipline that is similar in spirit to the type discipline for first-order ML modules; - The higher-order type discipline can be used to give a semantics to the ML modules with multiple views; - The type discipline for higher-order modules has the principal signature property.
the Damas-Miller type inference algorithm can be extended to handle higher-order module signatures, and that this extension has the desirable property that it preserves principal signatures.

the development of a type discipline for higher-order ML modules, which is as simple as possible, and yet is powerful enough to capture the semantics of the language.
the development of a type system for higher-order modules, which is compatible with a first-order type system for modules, and which has principal types for all expressions.

the higher-order ML module system is not a conservative extension of the ML module system.

we have extended the Damas-Mirner type system for higher-order functional languages to a first-class type system for higher order modules.
we have shown how the type system of a higher-order module system can be made to be decidable, and how the type system can be made compatible with the semantics.
we have extended the notion of principal types to the setting of higher-order modules, and we have shown that the notion of principal signature can be extended to the higher-order case.

higher-order module languages can have principal signatures, and that the type discipline for first-order module systems can be extended to a type discipline for higher-order module systems.
